articles.title: TfL earns £1.1 million from Turkish Airlines’ Elizabeth line advertising deal
articles.excerpt: You might have seen some large adverts appearing on the Elizabeth line recently, and they’re all part of a year-long campaign promoting Turkish Airlines. The campaign mixes banners at the bottom of st
articles.imageAlt: TfL earns £1.1 million from Turkish Airlines’ Elizabeth line advertising deal
articles.body:
You might have seen some large adverts appearing on the Elizabeth line recently, and they’re all part of a year-long campaign promoting Turkish Airlines. The campaign mixes banners at the bottom of station roundels with, in some places, very wide banners showing fictional timetables in a sort of tube moquette colour scheme. It’s now been confirmed that Transport for London (TfL) is earning £1.1 million from the campaign. In exchange, the airline gets its banners on up to 60 roundels across the Elizabeth line. They can also apply their vinyl to up to 60 platform benches at Bond Street, Tottenham Court Road and Liverpool Street stations. They can also add Turkish Airlines branding to some of the line diagram maps in the 15 Elizabeth line managed stations and host a one-day pop-up display at each station. One small change that’s worth pointing out is that the seats used to have ghostbuster vinyls on the walls, which are now covered up by the adverts. That also means the priority seat sign on the wall has been covered up. So a floor vinyl has replaced it, and arguably it’s more noticeable than the old sign had been. There may even be a long-term benefit, if the glue in the vinyls absorbs some dirt and removes it when the adverts are peeled off. Giant nasal pore strips for the tube. In the meantime, expect lots of Turkish Airlines adverts on the Lizzie line. Emma Strain, Customer Director at TfL, said: “This year-long collaboration with Turkish Airlines is part of our wider work to engage with brands, and creatively shows how our services connect people not just here but across the world. All the revenue raised though collaborations like this is invested into London’s transport network to provide further improvements across the capital.”

Source: Ian Visits

articles.title: Costain appoints new head to deliver HS2 tunnels
articles.excerpt: Costain has appointed Rohan O’Grady as the new managing directior of Skanska Costain STRABAG joint venture delivering the London tunnels section of HS2. O’Grady will take up his new role next mo
articles.imageAlt: Costain appoints new head to deliver HS2 tunnels
articles.body:
Costain has appointed Rohan O’Grady as the new managing directior of Skanska Costain STRABAG joint venture delivering the London tunnels section of HS2. O’Grady will take up his new role next month replacing Jonathan Morris who has served as interim MD for the last six months and will now be taking a sabbatical. O’Grady joins Costain from Australian based CPB Contractors where he oversaw a string of major infrastructure projects. Jonathan Willcock, Managing Director, Transportation, at Costain, said: “With his enviable CV and a successful track record at delivering large-scale mega-projects for both the public and private sectors, Rohan will be an excellent addition to Costain and is perfectly placed to lead the fantastic team working as part of the SCS joint venture. “Under his leadership, HS2’s London tunnels will continue to be delivered safely and efficiently, which will be critical for the new high-speed railway that will add capacity to the network and drive UK prosperity for generations to come.” O’Grady added: “Costain has a unique heritage and a fantastic reputation for engineering excellence. I’m proud to be taking on the leadership of the SCS JV at such an important stage in the delivery of HS2. “This is a project of enormous national significance, and I’m looking forward to working with the world-class expertise and talent that runs throughout the SCS JV to maintain momentum, ensure safety and build on the strong foundations that are already in place.”

Source: Construction Enquirer

articles.title: Developers called up for £10bn Old Oak mega-scheme
articles.excerpt: London’s biggest brownfield regeneration scheme is being readied for take-off after public bodies struck a landmark land deal around HS2’s Old Oak Common station The Old Oak and Park Royal Development
articles.imageAlt: Developers called up for £10bn Old Oak mega-scheme
articles.body:
London’s biggest brownfield regeneration scheme is being readied for take-off after public bodies struck a landmark land deal around HS2’s Old Oak Common station The Old Oak and Park Royal Development Corporation has agreed heads of terms with government, the Department for Transport and Network Rail to pull 70 acres at Old Oak into a single public sector development site. The move gives the developer market a clear run at one of the UK’s largest regeneration plays, with plans for 8,000 homes, 200,000 sq m of commercial and community space, new parks and public realm, and 11,000 jobs. OPDC will now start a two-stage bid contest this month to find a development and investment partner for the £10bn scheme. The preferred partner is due to be picked by spring 2027. OPDC said the hub station, which will link HS2, the Elizabeth line, Great Western Main Line and Heathrow Express, would anchor a new canal-side district and major hub for tech, research and business in west London. The Public Land Agreement will combine OPDC land with Department for Transport-owned sites for the first time, creating a unified platform for planning, infrastructure and development. The deal follows £340m of Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government funding used by OPDC to assemble privately-owned land across Old Oak. A tender notice will go live on the OPDC website and Find a Tender Service from 28 May, giving interested teams access to the procurement portal and bid documents. Mayor of London Sadiq Khan said: “This landmark partnership with national government means the capital’s biggest brownfield site, Old Oak, can now deliver for Londoners, driving forward significant housing delivery and economic growth.” Dame Karen Buck, chair of OPDC, said: “Securing the land is a breakthrough moment for OPDC. “Our collaboration with national and London government has brought Old Oak together as a single, strategic development site — giving the market certainty and unlocking exceptional placemaking potential. “Now, we are seeking an exemplar joint-venture partner with the vision and capability to turn this ambition into reality.”

Source: Construction Enquirer
articles.author: Old Oak Town

articles.title: Old Oak Common Station Construction Progresses
articles.excerpt: Foundation work completed for the UK's largest newly built station, with platform installation underway.
articles.imageAlt: HS2 Construction
articles.body:
Foundation work has been completed for the UK's largest newly built station at Old Oak Common, with platform installation now underway.

HS2 Ltd confirmed that the first platform sections have been installed, marking a significant milestone in the construction programme. The station will have 14 platforms serving HS2 high-speed services, the Elizabeth Line, Great Western Mainline, and Heathrow Express.
articles.author: Old Oak Town

articles.title: First Phase Housing Development Approved
articles.excerpt: OPDC approves 500 new homes including 50% affordable housing in the Old Oak Mile development.
articles.imageAlt: New Housing
articles.body:
The Old Oak and Park Royal Development Corporation (OPDC) has approved the first phase of housing in the Old Oak Mile development, comprising 500 new homes with 50% designated as affordable housing.

Construction is expected to begin in 2026 with first residents moving in by 2028.
